status: pre-registered: the rules and the formulas are closed; the numbers that depend on the V05-06 windowed baseline are not frozen yet
results: none: this file records no measurement and claims no result

baseline.windowed: pending: no windowed attempt was presented by the display

preRegistration.measurementsBeforeThisFile: none: the file is committed before any comparative measurement
preRegistration.pin: tests/frontier-comparison-protocol.test.mjs holds the SHA-256 of this file without the frozenValue and frozenAt fields
preRegistration.freeze: a later act fills only the frozenValue and frozenAt of the entries of `thresholds`, once, together with the `congelado` criterion of V05-06 and before the first comparative execution; nothing else of this file changes and the pin does not move
preRegistration.amendments: any other change is an amendment: it is listed with its date, commit and reason in the Amendments section of the research note and as an entry of the top-level `amendments` list (date, what, why, the text it replaces and the comparative measurements made before it), the pin in the test is changed on purpose in the same commit, and no execution made under the previous text is mixed with the new one

amendments.what: The idle reference of a run, which the secondary outcome 'frames above twice the idle reference' counts against and the pacing clause of the `not-presented` rule compares with half of the refresh period, is the median (nearest rank) of the half-sums of the consecutive pairs of the per-frame values of the 600 idle frames, median((x[i] + x[i+1]) / 2) for i from 0 to n - 2, in the same quantity as the frames it is compared with (the CPU time per frame for the secondary outcome, the elapsed intervals between process frames for the pacing clause), in place of the median of those values. Five texts change: idleReference.rule, the id and label of the secondary outcome (frames-above-twice-idle-median becomes frames-above-twice-idle-reference), the idle step of the script, the not-presented invalidation rule and preRegistration.amendments, which now names this list. The thresholds, the primary outcome, the windows, the hypotheses, the statistics and the decision rule do not change.
amendments.why: The V05-06 windowed baseline found that, with the vsync on at 120 Hz, the 600 idle intervals of a window the display presents come in two alternating groups: about 300 under 4.17 ms and about 300 of 12 ms or more, two neighbours adding up to about 16.67 ms and the mean being about 8.33 ms. The median falls in one group or the other by a few samples. One presented attempt of the baseline was refused as unpaced with a median of 4.136 ms against the 4.167 ms required, with a mean of 8.333 ms and 5,106 of 5,110 frames drawn; the five accepted runs of the turn had medians from 4.421 to 13.177 ms, and in its run 3 (median 4.421 ms) 242 of 360 click frames were above twice the idle median only because the median was in the low group. The median of the half-sums of consecutive pairs was between 8.327 and 8.342 ms in the 16 attempts of 2026-10-09 whose intervals came in two groups, is about 0.6 ms in a loop that nothing paces (0.704 to 0.710 ms in the three unpaced attempts of 2026-10-08), and a single stall moves only two of the half-sums, which the mean would not survive. The two alternating groups are an effect of the intervals between process frames with the vsync on, not of the CPU time; the median of the half-sums of pairs is robust to them and to an isolated stall and, in a series with no groups, is practically its median (6.888 against 6.901 ms in a uniform loop, 0.704 against 0.706 ms in an unpaced one), so the same statistic serves both quantities. The pre-registered text defined the idle median over the CPU time of the idle frames and compared the same idle median with half of the refresh period, which is a quantity of intervals; the amendment names, for each use, the quantity that is compared. The primary outcome, the CPU time per frame, does not change. The table is in docs/research/frontier-baseline.md and the evidence in docs/evidence/idle-reference/.
amendments.before: idleReference.rule: "after the boot, 600 consecutive frames with the map and the HUD still and nothing injected; the median CPU time of those frames is the run's idle median, the reference of the frames above twice the idle median". Secondary outcome: id "frames-above-twice-idle-median", label "Frames of a window whose CPU time is above twice the run's idle median". runs.script, step idle: "600 frames with nothing injected: the idle median". Invalidation rule not-presented: "... or the loop was not paced (the idle median is under half of the refresh period read back)". preRegistration.amendments: "any other change is an amendment: it is listed with its date, commit and reason in the Amendments section of the research note, the pin in the test is changed on purpose in the same commit, and no execution made under the previous text is mixed with the new one".

amendments.what: Arm B's time-box gets its length, and the open item of the iPhone records the NO-GO of V05-09. Three texts change: decisionRule.partialReport.timeBox (the unit, arm C's measurement, the optimization pass and the total), the `arm-b` open item and the `iphone` open item. The arms, the hypotheses, the outcomes, the windows, the executions, the statistics, the thresholds and the categories of the decision rule do not change; the `iphone` block keeps its GO and NO-GO rules, and its NO-GO branch is the one that applies.
amendments.why: The pre-registration said that arm B's time-box is the same as arm C's plus one optimization pass and that its length is set and recorded before arm B starts, but it gave no unit, no measurement of C and no length for the pass. The unit is the active time of the subagents, the only effort of C that carries timestamps: the transcripts of the implementer of #82 and #93 (one agent, 7.35 h), of the implementer of #100 (5.12 h) and of the two researchers (0.12 h and 0.19 h), 12.78 h in all. The cut of 30 minutes is on a plateau: 12.78 h with 30 or 60 minutes, 11.62 h with 20 and 10.50 h with 10, because the gaps under it are native suites that ran for up to 25 minutes with no event, and the only gap above it (305 minutes) is the wait between the first slice and the second. C's 12.8 h also built the game side that B reuses (the event queue, the context in the snapshot, the input blocking under overlays and the probes), so B's box is generous, as a native HUD that is not a straw man needs. The pass is a quarter of C's because C had none and the protocol asks for one round, not a second implementation. The NO-GO of V05-09 was recorded on 2026-10-09 (docs/evidence/frontier-device/README.md, #102), and the `iphone` block already said that with a NO-GO the comparison covers macOS only.
amendments.before: decisionRule.partialReport.timeBox: "the same as arm C's plus one optimization pass; its length is set and recorded before arm B starts". open, id arm-b: "arm B (criterion `braco-b`) does not exist; its time-box has no length yet". open, id iphone: "the iPhone depends on the GO or NO-GO of V05-09".

hypotheses.label: Cost of the React Native HUD

hypotheses.expectation: a positive difference, because the HUD, Hermes, Yoga and the Control mount share the main thread with the game

hypotheses.label: Cost of the native Godot HUD
hypotheses.nature: estimate of a price: the difference and its 95% interval are reported for each window, with no category and no claim that the cost is absent

hypotheses.label: Is the React Native HUD better than the native Godot HUD
hypotheses.nature: confirmatory: it takes the decision rule, the four categories and the Holm guard
hypotheses.nullHypothesis: C is not better than B
hypotheses.alternative: C costs less CPU time per frame than B by more than the margin, in a window
hypotheses.nonInferiority: C is non-inferior to B in a window when the upper end of the 95% interval of C minus B is at most +margin
hypotheses.expectation: no gain in CPU time per frame; if a gain appears it is expected in the cost of change, not in the frame

windows.ends: the last frame before the frame that delivers frontier.turn_ended
windows.occurrences: one per turn: 100 in the soak

windows.occurrences: one per turn: 100 in the soak

windows.ends: the second frame after the starting frame, so each occurrence has 3 frames

idleReference.rule: after the boot, 600 consecutive frames with the map and the HUD still and nothing injected; the run's idle reference is the median (nearest rank) of the half-sums of the consecutive pairs of the per-frame values x[0..n-1] of those 600 frames, median((x[i] + x[i+1]) / 2) for i from 0 to n - 2, in the same quantity as the frames it is compared with: for the secondary outcome 'frames above twice the idle reference' the values are the CPU time per frame, read by the instrument of the primary outcome (thresholds.cpu-time-instrument); for the pacing clause of the not-presented rule the values are the elapsed intervals between process frames, as the windowed lane records them

primaryOutcome.label: CPU time per frame, 95th percentile, within each active window
primaryOutcome.quantity: the CPU time of the main thread for a process frame, read by one instrument that is the same in the three arms; never the interval between frames
primaryOutcome.perRun: for each execution and each window, the 95th percentile, by nearest rank (the rank ceil(95 n / 100) of the n sorted values), of the CPU time of the frames of the window's measured occurrences
primaryOutcome.armValue: the median over the executions of an arm of the per-run values
primaryOutcome.analysedApart: each window is analysed on its own; idle frames are outside the primary outcome so that they do not dilute the difference
primaryOutcome.vsync: valid with the vsync on or off, because it reads CPU time and not the interval between frames

vsync.otherwise: the band of FPS without a limit is N/A, with the reading recorded, and the primary outcome stays the CPU time per frame
vsync.refreshRate: DisplayServer.screen_get_refresh_rate() is read back and recorded, never assumed
vsync.missedFramesWithVsyncOn: open: Godot gives no presentation timestamps, so the band is N/A while no instrument exists, as in the V05-06 baseline

CPU time per frame, 99th percentile, per window
Frames of a window whose CPU time is above twice the run's idle reference (the median of the half-sums of consecutive pairs of the CPU time per frame of the idle window)

secondaryOutcomes.label: Resident memory of the process

Time to the interactive HUD

secondaryOutcomes.label: FPS without a limit, per window
secondaryOutcomes.observation: per execution, in the unlimited lane only, and only when the vsync mode reads back DISABLED

secondaryOutcomes.label: Size of the exported Release package

secondaryOutcomes.label: Cost of change: one new action for the Settler
secondaryOutcomes.observation: single: one implementation of the same request in each arm

runs.why12: the Latin square has three blocks, so a design balanced in position needs a multiple of 3 executions per arm: 12 is the smallest one at or above 10
runs.balance: each arm runs 12 times and 4 times in each position of a block; the order is fixed here and not drawn; first-order carry-over is not balanced and no claim rests on it

lanes.vsync: the project's default, read back and recorded
lanes.reads: every outcome except the FPS without a limit

lanes.vsync: requested DISABLED and read back with window_get_vsync_mode()
lanes.reads: the FPS without a limit, per window; the lane keeps the same sequence; if the reading is not DISABLED the lane is N/A and is not run further

fixed.machine: the same Mac for every execution of every arm
fixed.build: Release export, never Debug; the binary, the package and the script are hashed and every execution records the hashes
fixed.replay: the 12-turn replay of 73 intents, whose golden hash is the one fixed in tests/civ-lite-game-native.test.mjs
fixed.input: scripted game intents, identical in the three arms, delivered at the game's intent boundary; the only real clicks are the latency pass of B and C

runs.process: each execution is a fresh process that runs the script below once; no two executions overlap

script.does: starts the process and reads the time to the interactive HUD (B and C) from the engine's clock

600 frames with nothing injected: their CPU time per frame gives the idle reference of the secondary outcome, and the elapsed intervals between their process frames give the pacing check of the presented lane
the 12-turn replay; its golden hash must match; its frames are kept in the raw data and belong to no window
100 turns of scripted End Turn intents; the windows ai-phase and event-burst
24 warm-up and 50 measured consecutive selection intents through the seven contexts; the window context-switches

B and C only: 2 warm-up and 30 measured real clicks on HUD controls found by testID, injected through Input.parse_input_event and flushed as in the V05-06 baseline; the click to panel latency in frames
2 warm-up and 30 measured rounds of the stress scenario; the window stress
reads the resident memory, the SceneTree's nodes and, in C, the Hermes heap after a forced collection and the native views; records the exit code

runs.warmup: follows the V05-06 baseline: the first 2 occurrences of a window, flagged in the raw data and left out of every statistic; the context switches discard 24 (2 rounds of the baseline's 12-swap tour); the idle window of 600 frames is the baseline's

load.read: before the execution starts and after it ends, both recorded
load.overLimit: an execution with a 1-minute load average above the limit in either reading is redone
load.redo: the redone execution takes the place of the rejected one in the sequence; the rejected attempt stays in the raw data with its load readings and its reason; at most 3 attempts per slot, and when they are used up the campaign stops with that recorded and produces no statistic

runs.provenance: recorded for every execution: the commit, the machine, the system, the display, the renderer and the adapter, the vsync mode and the refresh rate read back, the load before and after, the hashes of the binary, the package and the script
runs.rawData: every frame of every execution, the warm-up flagged, and every rejected attempt, kept under docs/evidence/ so that anyone can apply another rule to the same data

statistics.perRun: percentiles by nearest rank, as the V05-06 baseline and the GF-30 oracle compute them

acrossRuns.center: the median of the per-run values (the mean of the two middle values when the number of values is even)
acrossRuns.spread: the interquartile range by nearest rank (ranks ceil(n / 4) and ceil(3 n / 4) of the sorted values)

statistics.contrast: the difference of the medians across the executions of two arms
statistics.intervals: three pairs times four windows: twelve primary intervals

interval.method: percentile bootstrap of the difference of the medians
interval.unitOfResampling: the execution, resampled with replacement and independently within each of the two arms, as many as the arm has
interval.stream: one generator per interval, seeded with the seed; for each resample, the draws of the minuend arm and then the draws of the subtrahend arm, each draw being floor(u n)
interval.bounds: the elements of rank 250 and 9750 of the 10,000 sorted differences

multiplicity.family: the four primary windows of H3 (C minus B)
multiplicity.pValues: for each window, the smallest of three one-sided bootstrap p-values, with d the resampled difference oriented so that negative is better: for gain, (1 + #{d >= -margin}) / (R + 1); for cost, (1 + #{d <= margin}) / (R + 1); for neutral, the larger of (1 + #{d <= -margin}) / (R + 1) and (1 + #{d >= margin}) / (R + 1); R is the number of resamples
multiplicity.procedure: sort the four p-values; the k-th smallest (k from 1) stands when it is at most alphaOneSided / (4 - k + 1) and every smaller one stood
multiplicity.effect: the guard only downgrades: a gain, cost or neutral verdict of a window whose claim does not stand is reported as inconclusive, with the unadjusted category and interval shown beside it; an inconclusive window stays inconclusive
multiplicity.outsideTheFamily: H1 and H2 are estimates; the secondary axes are read with their unadjusted intervals; neither is adjusted nor claims more than its interval says

statistics.outliers: none is discarded: the warm-up and the validity rules are the only rules that leave data out
statistics.analysis: run by a script committed before the first comparative execution; its output is reproducible from the raw data and the seed

decisionRule.scope: C against B, in each primary window and on each axis with `verdict: true`

margin.formula: max(relative x the median of B, floor)
margin.relativeTo: the median over the executions of B of the per-run value in that window
margin.source: the number comes from the measurement of B; only the formula is fixed here

decisionRule.orientation: for an outcome where higher is better the interval [lo, hi] of C minus B is negated to [-hi, -lo] before the categories apply, so that a gain always means better

categories.means: C is better than B beyond the margin
the whole interval lies within the margin
C is worse than B beyond the margin
the interval crosses -margin or +margin: too wide to decide, reported as such and never rounded to neutral

nonInferior.reportedAs: a flag beside the category, never in place of it: an interval that crosses only -margin is inconclusive and non-inferior

decisionRule.fpsGain: a gain in FPS is stated only when the interval excludes zero; a gain by the rule above already does
decisionRule.perAxis: every axis with `verdict: true` gets one category; the frame time axis gets one for each of the four windows, which the report shows side by side and never averages

singleObservation.rule: one implementation per arm, so there is no interval: the category is taken on the difference of each of files, lines, time and tests against the margin (gain below -margin, cost above +margin, neutral within), the axis takes it only when the four agree and is inconclusive otherwise, and the report says it is one observation per arm and supports a description and not a statistical claim

deterministic.rule: the repeated export gives equal sizes, so the interval is the point: the category is taken on the difference of the two sizes against the margin; if the two exports of an arm differ the axis is inconclusive

decisionRule.absoluteBudget: once frozen, the median over the executions of an arm of the per-run p95 of a window is compared with the window's budget (met when at most the budget, exceeded otherwise, N/A while the budget is null); it is reported beside the category for B and for C and never changes the category

partialReport.when: arm B is not ready in its time-box
partialReport.report: a partial comparison of A against C: H1 only, no category for H3 and no gain claimed
partialReport.timeBox: the same as arm C's plus one optimization pass, counted as the active time of the subagents that implement and research the arm: the sum of the gaps shorter than 30 minutes between consecutive timestamped events of their transcripts (a longer gap is a wait for review or for a decision, not work). Arm C, the React Native HUD of V05-05 (#82, #93 and #100), took 12.8 h by that count. Arm B therefore has 12.8 h to pass the context matrix (the invalidation rule `parity`), then one optimization pass of at most 3.2 h (a quarter of C's): one round, after the parity passes, that profiles arm B alone by idiomatic Godot means, outside any comparative execution, and keeps the parity. In all 16.0 h, counted the same way from the first event of arm B's first subagent; recorded on 2026-10-09, before arm B starts

thresholds.rule: one engine-side reading of the main thread's CPU time for the process frame, taken by the same code in the three arms, that excludes the wait for the display; a self-check with a synthetic load of known duration must read it within 10% before any comparative execution
thresholds.source: the instrument self-check of V05-10 `execucao`; the host's pump accounting is not used because arms A and B have no host

frozenValue.quantity: total_ms = physics_ms + process_ms + setup_ms + render_ms for each process frame, in milliseconds: the monotonic elapsed time between the engine's hooks on the main thread (not the thread's CPU clock of the operating system), every term ending before the frame is presented; the percentile and the windows are the protocol's
frozenValue.reading: Time.get_ticks_usec stamped at SceneTree.process_frame, RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw (the last _process when the frame does not draw), SceneTree.physics_frame and the last _physics_process; RenderingServer.get_frame_setup_time_cpu() and viewport_get_measured_render_time_cpu() read at frame_post_draw, with the render measure on for the main window's viewport; never Performance.TIME_PROCESS or TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS, which are a once-a-second maximum and, for TIME_PROCESS with the vsync on, hold the wait for the display (TIME_PROCESS stays in the samples as a cross-check)
frozenValue.alignment: the render reading of a draw is the one taken 6 draws later (Compatibility renderer, Godot 4.7.2, macOS), joined by draw index when the run is over; the harness keeps 6 draws after the last window it needs, and the lag is checked by the render pulse every time the lab probe runs
frozenValue.observedError: against a load of known duration, at most 0.16% at 2, 5, 10 and 20 ms headless and at most 1.5% in a presented window (the 2 ms load; 0.22% or less in the others), under the 10% rule; the instrument's floor, the idle total, is about 0.014 ms headless and 0.082 ms in a window, the same in every arm
frozenValue.gate: the protocol's `instrument` rule is operational as: tests/cpu-time-instrument.gd is byte-identical to the one the probe and the oracle passed (its hash goes in the provenance), and the probe and the oracle are rerun on the machine, the engine and the renderer of the campaign before it starts

thresholds.rule: the median across five presented runs of the window's p95 plus three times its interquartile range, rounded up to 0.5 ms, as the V05-06 proposal derives a presented frame time
thresholds.source: V05-06 `turno`: the frame time of a turn with the AI sliced per frame

thresholds.rule: the same rule, on the frames of the end of a turn
thresholds.source: V05-06 `turno`: the frame time of the end of a turn

thresholds.rule: the same rule, on the swap frame p95 of the presented windowed baseline
thresholds.source: V05-06 windowed baseline: swap frame p95, pending until a display presents the window

thresholds.rule: the same rule, on the stress scenario's counterpart in V05-06; frozen as N/A with the reason when V05-06 measured none, and then the window is judged by the relative rule alone
thresholds.source: V05-06 `turno` or `soak`, whichever measured a log of 200 lines and a production list of 100 items
thresholds.frozenValue: N/A: V05-06 measured no log of 200 lines and no production list of 100 items (the turn's tour and the soak's 100 turns keep the game's state small), so the stress window is judged by the relative rule alone

invalidation.rule: the 1-minute load average above the written limit before or after the execution

in the presented lane, the window did not draw throughout (a frame drawn after every measured intent and in at least nine of ten frames of the idle window) or the loop was not paced (the idle reference, the median of the half-sums of consecutive pairs of the elapsed intervals between process frames of the idle window, is under half of the refresh period read back)
invalidation.action: reject with the reason, keep the raw data and redo

invalidation.rule: a Debug build, or a binary, package or script whose hash differs from the registered one, or a seed that is not the registered one
the golden hash of the 12-turn replay or the final hash of the soak differs from the registered one
invalidation.action: reject and redo; a repeat of it in one arm stops the campaign

invalidation.rule: an unhandled JavaScript error, a script error or an error in Godot's log, a crash, or an exit code that is not 0
in B or C, the visible testIDs differ from the table of the context matrix in any of the seven contexts
invalidation.action: reject and redo; arm B is not ready until it passes

invalidation.rule: in the unlimited lane, the vsync mode does not read back DISABLED
invalidation.action: not invalid: the FPS band is N/A for that execution, with the reading recorded

invalidation.rule: a window has fewer measured occurrences than its protocol number
the instrument's self-check was not passed, or the reading changed after it
invalidation.action: no comparative execution counts until it is repeated and passed

iphone.rule: the same measurements with the same windows and statistics; the effective refresh rate is recorded; if the vsync cannot be disabled there the unlimited lane is N/A and the CPU time per frame and the headroom against the refresh period with the vsync on are the outcome

open.text: the presented windowed baseline of V05-06 is pending, and `turno`, `soak` and `congelado` are open, so the absolute budgets are formulas with a null value
arm B (criterion `braco-b`) does not exist yet; its time-box is set in decisionRule.partialReport.timeBox (the amendment of 2026-10-09 that records it)
the exact reading of the CPU time per frame is chosen and checked by `execucao` before the first comparative execution and then frozen
missed frames with the vsync on need presentation timestamps that Godot does not give
V05-09 is a NO-GO (2026-10-09), so by the `iphone` block the comparison covers macOS only
the scenario script, the analysis script and the hashes of the binary and the package are written by `execucao` and `relatorio`, before the first comparative execution
